question: To develop scientific temper and humanism is a:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fundamental Duty.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Developing scientific temper and humanism is a** fundamental duty** of every citizen of India.
 
• It is one of the ten fundamental duties enshrined in the **Indian Constitution under Article 51A.**
 
• This duty aims to promote the** spirit of inquiry, rationality, and scientific temper** among citizens, which is essential for the progress of the nation.
 
• Humanism refers to the philosophy that emphasizes the **value and agency of human beings**, individually and collectively, and generally prefers critical thinking and evidence over acceptance of dogma or superstition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Every citizen in India has the right to** constitutional remedies**, including equality before the** law and equal protection** of the laws, as guaranteed by **Articles 226 and 32 **of the Indian Constitution. 
 
• The following list of the **Indian Constitution's six fundamental rights** and the related constitutional articles includes: **Equal Rights (Articles 14–18) Freedom of Speech (Articles 19–22) Right not to be exploited (Articles 23–24) Right to Religious Freedom (Articles 25–28).**
 
• The directive principles of state policy are covered in **Part IV **of our constitution **(Articles 36–51)**.
 
• It entails a number of things, such as the adoption of a **uniform civil code**, the elimination of legal restrictions on women, the outlawing of untouchability in all forms, and more
